thread:
Matt: Heads-up — ApexHealth sent back the CAIQ and highlighted key/mgmt and data residency bits. They want a concise shared-responsibility table and short canned answers for the questionnaire. Can we draft something quick for the proposal? cc @Erin @Julia

Erin: On it. Do we have a preferred phrasing for KMS/HSM ownership vs customer-managed keys in Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted?

Julia: Short answer: Hosted = Redwood-managed keys by default (we can support customer KMS for enterprise add-on), Dedicated = customer-managed KMS supported via Bring-Your-Key config, Private/on-prem = customer KMS/HSM in their VPC or HSM.

Sam: +1. For CAIQ Q about cryptographic key lifecycle (QAL-1 style) we should state who does rotation, where logs live, and access controls. Suggest 3-line answer: what we do, what customer controls, and a link to the key management doc.

Matt: Great. Can someone paste a tiny ownership matrix we can drop into the CAIQ or the security questionnaire spreadsheet? They want it inline (not just a link).

Erin: Here — quick table, keeping it very short. Feel free to trim for the CAIQ cell limits.

```
Control area | Redwood responsibility | Customer responsibility
---|---|---
Key management (Hosted) | Key storage, rotation, access control (Redwood KMS) | Data classification, access requests, application-level encryption keys
Key management (Dedicated/Private) | Enable BYK support, operate runtime; optional key rotation tooling | Provide/rotate KMS keys (Cloud KMS / HSM), manage HSM network ACLs
Logging & audit | Ingest infra logs, provide audit exports; SOC2 monitoring | Retain application logs, manage PIIs; configure log-forwarding to customer SIEM (if required)
Data residency & backups | Can pin region for hosted; backup encryption | Provide site-specific compliance requirements, accept egress constraints
```

Julia: That looks fine. For CAIQ we should map specific controls to product features, e.g., CCM-09 (Key mgmt) -> Hosted: Redwood KMS; Dedicated: BYK support; Private: customer HSM. Also mention support for KMS integrations: GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM via PKCS#11.

Matt: Can we add a one-liner for evidence artifacts? They asked what we can provide during vendor review.

Sam: Draft: "Evidence available on request: SOC2 Type II report, KMS configuration screenshots, key rotation logs, architecture diagram showing KMS/HSM boundaries, and a dedicated controls mapping spreadsheet."

Erin: I'll paste a CAIQ-style canned answer for Q about shared responsibility (short):

"Redwood Inference operates the inference platform and underlying infrastructure components. Customers are responsible for application-level data handling, tenant-level access control, and management of customer-provided cryptographic keys in Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted deployments, Redwood manages default encryption keys but supports customer-managed keys under enterprise agreements. Detailed responsibilities and evidence options are listed in the attached controls matrix."

Julia: Perfect. Add a note about PII handling: "We do not use customer data to train models. PII processing follows customer configuration and retention policies; portable exports and deletion APIs available."

infra-security-bot: Security doc link added: https://internal.redwood.dev/security/vendor-reviews/apexhealth-reqs (permissions: sales+sec) :white_check_mark:

Matt: Thank you. Last ask — pricing/POC: customer wants Dedicated POC w/ BYK enabled for a 2-week evaluation. Can we confirm any additional setup fees or timeline? Erin/Sam?

Sam: Typical timeline: 1 week infra prep (capacity + network), 2-3 days for KMS/HSM integration testing, then POC run. Setup fee: depends on GPU reservation size; estimate in the quote. I'll flag exact numbers in the proposal doc.

Erin: I'll drop the final copy into the CAIQ spreadsheet and ping legal for the BYK addendum. Planning to send to customer by EOD unless anyone objects.

Matt: No objections. Thanks team — will include the matrix and canned answers in the security questionnaire response. :thumbsup:
